== Biography ==
Hugh Glasgow was probably born about 1705. This estimate is reportedly based on an inscription on a Glasgow family gravestone in St Cedma's churchyard, Larne.<ref>[[Space:Chronology_of_the_Glasgow_Family_in_Northern_Ireland_in_Historical_Context|Chronology of the Glasgow Family in Northern Ireland in Historical Context]].</ref>

=== Residence and property in Larne ===

On 10 March 1736, Hugh Glasgow and [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]], both of Larne, County Antrim, received a lease from Alexander, Earl of Antrim. Memorial 63221 was registered on 10 April 1738 at eleven in the morning.<ref name="lease">Registry of Deeds, Dublin, memorial 63221, lease dated 10 March 1736; registered 10 April 1738. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSN1-FXR2 FamilySearch image 542], image group 008088380, volumes 87–88; original image inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

The lease covered two tenements already in their possession on the north side of the street in Newtown, Larne. One had a frontage of 23 feet, bounded east by Mr Agnew's tenement and west by Robert Robinson's. The other had a frontage of 32 feet, bounded east by John Boyd's tenement and west by John White's. Both extended backwards 150 feet.<ref name="lease" />

The annual rent was £1 16 shillings sterling, with receiver's fees of two pence per pound. The term began on the preceding 1 November and was measured by the lives of George II, Frederick Prince of Wales and Prince William Augustus Duke of Cumberland, with provision for replacement lives. The named lives were royal family members, not Glasgow children.<ref name="lease" />

The lease witnesses were James Stenhouse of Larne and William Harrison, clerk to Alexander Stewart of Ballylough. Stenhouse and Robert Wilson of Larne, merchant, witnessed the memorial. Stenhouse proved execution at Carrickfergus on 28 March 1738, stating that Alexander Stewart had executed the lease in the Earl's name and that William and Hugh had executed the lease and memorial.<ref name="lease" />

The memorial names no parent, spouse or child of either lessee and states no relationship between them. The later renewal endorsements remain separate research targets.

=== Joint lessors named in a 1757 assignment ===

A deed poll dated 4 June 1757, Matthew Stewart of Carncastle, farmer, to Robert Rainey of Larne, weaver, concerned a conditional assignment for £20 of Stewart's interest in a lease granted by [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]] of Larne. The original memorial does not date their head lease or describe the holding sufficiently to identify it with the 1736 Newtown tenements.<ref name="JointLessors1757">Registry of Deeds, memorial 159181, manuscript pp. 473–474, deed dated 4 June 1757, registered 26 May 1761; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJM-MJX4 FamilySearch image 257, opening] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJM-MJP6 image 258, continuation], original images inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

The joint names and Larne locality strongly support association with these lessees, but the record names no Glasgow relative or relationship between William and Hugh. Neither Glasgow executed this assignment; its registration in 1761 does not prove that either was then living. The separate 1751 and 1767 endorsements to the 1736 lease remain unexamined and may identify replacement lives.<ref>PRONI D2977/3A/4/81/72A, 1736 William and Hugh Glasgow lease with 1751 and 1767 endorsements; [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/eCatNI_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI eCatalogue], catalogue description only.</ref>

=== Church ===

A family chronology states that Hugh Glasgow became an elder of the Larne and Kilwaughter Presbyterian congregation in 1741.<ref>[[Space:Chronology_of_the_Glasgow_Family_in_Northern_Ireland_in_Historical_Context|Chronology of the Glasgow Family in Northern Ireland in Historical Context]].</ref>

A nineteenth-century account quoting the Larne Session Book includes Hugh Glasgow among the members of the Session and records that he died on 8 July 1767.<ref name="death">[https://archive.org/stream/christianunitari0003unse/christianunitari0003unse_djvu.txt “Congregational Memoirs—Larne and Kilwaughter,”] ''The Christian Unitarian'', vol. 3 (1864), p. 197. The account quotes the Larne Session Book entry: “Hugh Glasgow … dead July 8, 1767.”</ref>

Hugh therefore died on 8 July 1767, provided that the elder named in the Session Book was the same Hugh Glasgow who held the 1736 Larne lease.<ref name="death" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Father confidence review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-1502]] is assessed at 28% (uncertain). The older Robert-1502 represented the Larne/Kilwaughter congregation in1700–01; Hugh’s later Larne household supplies locality and a plausible succeeding generation. This is a coherent existing local-family hypothesis. Neither Hugh’s deeds nor his monument names Robert as father; the birth estimates are correlated tree premises, and collateral kin remain viable.

Existing father hypothesis only. Hugh’s documented wife, children and property establish his own household, not this upstream parent.

Next useful test: Seek a succession or kinship clause in the existing Larne lease/title chain; do not reread unrelated national indexes.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-1499 Chronology of the Glasgow Family in Northern Ireland in Historical Context.]. No new original was inspected in this review. This is an assessment of an existing attachment, not a new father.


=== Preferred father of the Larne ropemaker ===
James [[Glasgow-1509]], the older Larne ropemaker, is now selected as a possible son,52%, from the reported1737/1762 family account and the Glasgow–Shutter network. The younger James-3991 remains separate. Ann is not newly assigned as mother.

Select Hugh [[Glasgow-1499]] as the preferred possible father of James [[Glasgow-1509]], the older Belfast/Larne ropemaker, at 52% subjective confidence, replacing William [[Glasgow-1505]] in the local working tree. The archived chronology explicitly places a James, son of Hugh, at New Town/Larne in 1737 and identifies its reported 1762 Janet Shutter groom with that James. Hugh is an independently documented Larne merchant and elder, jointly leasing Newtown property in1736 and dealing with Hugh Shutter in the original1749 mortgage. The later James/Janet account and the distinctive Jane Shutter name in the younger William’s monument fit a recurring Glasgow–Shutter network. These combined named-parent, locality, generation and family-association clues favour Hugh over retaining a William father without a named-son record.

This is a preferred working identification, not a proved father clause for the adult ropemaker. The chronology is one derivative reconstruction: its1737 child,1762 groom and reported1737–1802 stone must not be counted as three independent confirmations. The adult’s1737 birth may itself derive from that reconstruction; the independent1773 affidavit establishes only birth before27 October1743. The original1737 entry,1762 marriage and alleged James/Janet stone remain uninspected. Hugh Shutter’s relationship to Janet is unknown, and a business association does not identify a father-in-law. A different Hugh remains possible. No mother is selected: Ann is not established as the1737 child’s mother by the reviewed account.

The monument’s separately recorded James [[Glasgow-3991]], son of Hugh and Ann, died in1812 aged64 and belongs to the younger1747/48 generation. That is a serious rival explanation: the reported1737 child could have died and the name been used again. It is not a recorded death of that earlier child. Withdraw the categorical earlier inference that the1737 James must have died young. Do not equate the two James profiles, invent a second wife, or infer surviving brothers with the same forename as an established fact. The older ropemaker was already an adult in1760–1761 and over thirty in1773, so he remains distinct from the younger monument/tanner comparison.

Retain William [[Glasgow-1505]] as an unselected uncertain father alternative at27%, preserving his earlier possible but individually unrated placement. A William Glasgow, Larne merchant, witnessed the1760 ropewalk lease, which is genuine positive association with James; the witness is not expressly called his father and may be the older William or another adult namesake. William and Hugh’s joint1736/1757 property activity makes a wider family or business relationship plausible without choosing its degree. William could be father, uncle or another associate. The specific reported Hugh-son identification and Hugh–Shutter connection now favour Hugh, but do not exclude William. The percentages express comparative research judgment, not a measured frequency or independent-source calculation.

One selected father is replaced locally. The child-side working branch contains49 retained pre-1850 profile accounts, including James and uncertain descendants; their own grades are unchanged. This is not49 new or proved relationships. The men were already in the same working component, so no component merger or new genealogical connection is claimed. No vital date, place, spouse, mother, identity merge or live WikiTree field changes. Hugh’s own uncertain ancestry and James’s Inishrush descendants retain their prior assessments.

The next discriminators are the original1737 entry,1762 marriage, full James/Janet monument and any surviving1737-child death or later household recital. The1760 William witness must be identified separately rather than silently assigned to the older William. A document naming a parent, sibling or inherited holding would test the preferred model; its absence is not an automatic exclusion.<ref name="LarnePreferredFather">[https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html Donna Jean Glasgow, Life’s Weaving, archived Kilwaughter/Larne chronology, 1737 and1762 entries; reread18 October2026; derivative reconstruction, original register and reported stone not inspected]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-7XCG Registry of Deeds memorial97407, mortgage6 November1749, FamilySearch image449; original reading of21 September2026 reused]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-S7XZ-8 Registry of Deeds,10 September1760 Gardenmore ropewalk lease, registered24 November1763; maintained original reading reused]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-M72W-M Registry affidavit27 October1773, registered15 November: James of Larne aged upwards of thirty; maintained original reading reused]; [https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up Bigger and Hughes, Larne churchyard inscriptions, Ulster Journal of Archaeology, second series6, pp.47–48; previously inspected published monument transcription reused].</ref>





=== Possible son John of Larne ===

[[Glasgow-4179|John Glasgow]], who married [[Allan-6611|Rose Allan]] at Larne in 1769, is a possible son, with low confidence. His estimated birth about 1747 fits Hugh's age and Larne household, but the marriage chronology does not name John's father.<ref>Donna Jean Glasgow, [https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html Kilwaughter and Larne Glasgow chronology], entry for John Glasgow and Rose Allan's 1769 marriage. The birth estimate of 1745–48 is the compiler's estimate.</ref> The relationship is a working hypothesis and is marked uncertain. [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]] remains an alternative father. No evidence establishes that Hugh's wife Ann was John's mother.

The Larne memorial gives Hugh's death as 8 July 1767 aged 62 and commemorates members of his family, but does not name John. It has not been established as a complete enumeration of surviving children, so the omission neither proves nor excludes the proposed relationship.<ref>''Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim'', ''Ulster Journal of Archaeology'', [https://archive.org/stream/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala_djvu.txt Glasgow stone at Larne], pp. 47–48.</ref> Further tests include the original registers (PRONI MIC/1B/6) and the renewal endorsements to the 1736 lease (PRONI D2977/3A/4/81/72A).


=== Possible duplicate ===

This profile may represent the same person as [[Glasgow-548|Hugh Glasgow (abt.1706-abt.1760)]]. A merger should not be completed until the conflicting death information and the other relationships attached to the two profiles have been examined. The Larne Session Book supports a death date of 8 July 1767 rather than about 1760.<ref name="death" />

=== Possible Dublin baptism ===

A Hugh Glascoe was baptised in Dublin in 1704, the son of William Glascoe and Jone.<ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FR3H-8L7 FamilySearch record for Hugh Glascoe].</ref>

No evidence currently establishes that the child baptised in Dublin was the later Hugh Glasgow of Larne. The similar name and approximate date are not enough by themselves to identify them as the same person.

=== 1740 Protestant householder ===

A Hugh Glasgow appears in the 1740 list of Protestant householders for Tamlaght O'Crilly Parish.<ref>[https://www.virtualtreasury.ie/item/PRONI-T808-15258 Virtual Treasury of Ireland, PRONI T808/15258, Names of Protestant Householders, 1740].</ref>

The identification is uncertain. The 1736 lease places Hugh Glasgow in Larne, and the church evidence also associates a man of that name with Larne. The Tamlaght O'Crilly entry should therefore remain a possible identification, not a confirmed event in his life.

=== Duneane surname ambiguity ===
The 1740 Duneane return includes Henry Glads. The reading may represent another surname and is not securely Glasgow. It is retained only as east-Antrim surname context and is not evidence that Henry was this Hugh or a relative.<ref>[https://www.billmacafee.com/1740returns/1740protestantreturnsantrim.pdf Underlying record source: henry glads duneane 1740].</ref>

=== Mortgage with Hugh Shutter, 1749 ===

A mortgage dated 6 November 1749 records William Eakine of Larne conveying Old Town premises as security to Hugh Shutter and Hugh Glasgow. Hugh Glasgow is described as a merchant of Larne and executed the memorial. The underlying lease was dated 11 August 1748.<ref name="HughMortgage1749">Registry of Deeds, memorial 97407, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-7XCG FamilySearch image 449], original manuscript inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

Place, date and occupation strongly favour this Hugh. The deed establishes a Glasgow–Shutter business association before the reported 1762 marriage of [[Glasgow-1509|James Glasgow]] to Janet Shutter, but names no relationship and proves neither that marriage nor Hugh’s parentage of James or [[Glasgow-4179|John Glasgow]].
